Exercise A

Jake's Life in the Midwest

Read the text carefully, then answer the questions below.

Read the text

Jake is fourteen years old and lives in Milwaukee, Wisconsin — a city on the shore of Lake Michigan, one of the five Great Lakes. Milwaukee is in the American Midwest, a large region of flat land, farms and friendly people.

Jake goes to Lincoln Middle School. His school day starts at 7:45 a.m. and finishes at 2:30 p.m. He takes a yellow school bus every morning. At school, he studies English, maths, science, social studies and art. His favourite subject is science because they do lots of experiments. After school, he plays basketball in the school gym or goes to drama club.

In November, Jake's family celebrates Thanksgiving. It is one of the most important holidays in the USA. Jake's mum cooks a big turkey with mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce and pumpkin pie. The whole family comes together — grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins. Before they eat, everyone says what they are thankful for. Jake always says he is thankful for his dog, Buddy.

In summer, Jake's family often drives to the shore of Lake Michigan. They go swimming, build sandcastles and have barbecues. Jake says the lake is so big that it looks like the sea. "You can't see the other side!" he tells his friends in Germany.

Answer the questions
1. Where does Jake live?
2. How does Jake get to school?
3. What is Jake's favourite subject?
4. What does Jake's family eat at Thanksgiving?
5. What does Jake say he is thankful for?
6. What does the family do at Lake Michigan in summer?
Exercise B

Simple Present — Daily Routines

Complete each sentence with the correct simple present form of the verb in brackets. Remember: he/she/it adds -s or -es.

Grammar reminder

We use the simple present for things that happen regularly or are always true.

I/you/we/they → base form: I play basketball.

He/she/it → add -s or -es: She plays basketball. He watches TV.

Negative: I don't like… / He doesn't like…

Fill in the gaps
1. Jake _____ to school at 7:30 every morning. (go)
2. His school day _____ at 2:30 p.m. (finish)
3. Jake and his friends _____ basketball after school. (play)
4. His mum _____ a big turkey at Thanksgiving. (cook)
5. The family _____ to the lake every summer. (drive)
6. Jake _____ science because they do experiments. (like)
7. The students _____ English, maths and art at school. (study)
8. Jake's dog Buddy _____ in the garden every afternoon. (run)
Exercise C

Present Progressive — What's Happening Now?

It is Thanksgiving Day at Jake's house. Choose the correct present progressive form to describe what everyone is doing right now.

Grammar reminder

We use the present progressive (also called present continuous) for things happening right now or at this moment.

Form: am / is / are + verb-ing

I am watching TV. / She is cooking dinner. / They are playing outside.

Fill in the gaps
1. Jake's mum _____ the turkey in the kitchen. (prepare)
2. Jake and his brother _____ the table for dinner. (set)
3. Grandma _____ pumpkin pie in the oven. (bake)
4. The cousins _____ a football game on TV. (watch)
5. Dad _____ with Uncle Tom about the football scores. (talk)
6. Buddy the dog _____ under the kitchen table. (sleep)
7. Jake _____ cranberry sauce on the turkey. (put)
8. Everyone _____ because they are thankful for the meal. (smile)
Exercise D

Writing — My School Day & Right Now

Write two short paragraphs (6–8 sentences total). Use the simple present in the first paragraph and the present progressive in the second.

What to write

Paragraph 1 — My typical school day (simple present): What time do you get up? How do you get to school? What subjects do you have? What do you do after school?

Paragraph 2 — Right now (present progressive): What are you doing at this moment? What are your classmates doing? Is anyone talking or laughing?

Helpful phrases
Simple present: I get up at… I go to school by… My first lesson starts at… I usually eat… After school, I…
Present progressive: I am sitting… We are doing… My teacher is… My friend is writing… Right now, I…
